SK5005 A broken cipher, or a mode that leaks structure

DES, TripleDES, RC2 or ECB mode — none of them hides a plaintext any more.

CategorySecurity
Default severityerror
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.1

Why

DES has a 56-bit key, which was already marginal when it was standardised and is exhaustively searched in hours on hardware anyone can rent. TripleDES fixed the key length and not the 64-bit block, so a collision becomes likely after about 32 GB under one key and the plaintext starts coming back out — that is CVE-2016-2183, "Sweet32", and it is a practical attack on a long TLS connection rather than a theoretical one. RC2 has practical key-recovery attacks. ECB is a different failure and a more visible one: it encrypts equal blocks to equal ciphertext, so the shape of the input survives encryption — the standard demonstration is a bitmap of a penguin that is still obviously a penguin afterwards. Use Aes, and prefer AesGcm, which authenticates the ciphertext as well as hiding it, so an attacker cannot flip bits in a message you will decrypt and act on. ⚠ There is no fix, and that is deliberate: swapping the algorithm compiles and changes the key length, the block size and the ciphertext format, so everything already encrypted becomes unreadable. That is a data migration, not an edit.

Example

Instead of:

using var cipher = TripleDES.Create();
cipher.Mode = CipherMode.ECB;
cipher.Key = key;

Write:

using var cipher = Aes.Create();
cipher.Mode = CipherMode.CBC;
cipher.Key = key;
cipher.GenerateIV();

When it does not fire

⚠ The id was allocated narrower than docs/plan/08's sentence for it, and the reason is that the other half cannot be decided correctly. The catalogue wrote "weak hash/cipher (MD5, SHA1, DES, ECB)" and the hash half was cut — not for firing too often, which would be work for the repository rather than a defect in the rule, but because the finding would frequently be wrong. MD5 and SHA-1 have a large legitimate population in which they are not security controls at all: cache keys, ETags, content addressing, bucket selection, and every wire protocol that froze its digest choice a decade ago and specifies it normatively — an RFC 6455 WebSocket handshake is defined as a SHA-1 of the client key and a fixed GUID, and reporting it would assert a vulnerability in code that cannot have one. Separating that population from a password digest needs to know what the hash is compared against and what happens when it matches, which is a question about the value's use that this rule does not ask and that an intra-procedural engine could not answer if it did. ADR-012 forbids widening an id later, so the hash half needs its own number — and an argument about how it will decide the question — before it is built. What ships fires only on a type deriving from DES, TripleDES or RC2, and on CipherMode.ECB as the value assigned to a cipher's Mode, so if (algorithm.Mode == CipherMode.ECB) throw is silent: that is the guard, not the bug. A DES implementation kept only to decrypt an old archive is a true finding and an unwelcome one; that is what a baseline entry is for, and it is not a reason to soften the rule.
